ambiguities_or_notes: Every source block (26) has a matching target block, with page markers, numbering, quotation structure, and italics preserved.

Website Circle of Reading paragraphs served as the first draft; each was re-read against the Russian and revised where it drifted (omissions, additions, generic he/his, terminology, attribution form).

The council formula «изволися нам и святому духу» (izvolisya nam i svyatomu dukhu, Acts 15:28 in Church Slavonic) is rendered in a slightly archaic register, “it hath pleased us and the holy spirit,” lowercase as printed. «Гербер Ньютон» (Gerber N'yuton) is Heber Newton (not the website's 'Herbert'), «Иоанн Гус» (Ioann Gus) John Hus, and the marshal «фон-Поппенгейм» (fon-Poppengeym) is transliterated as printed, 'von Poppenheim' (historically Haupt von Pappenheim).
Source observation: [10] the year 1682 is printed for Leighton's punishment, which took place in 1630; translated as printed (a source error, not a transcription slip)
Source observation: [19] «фон-Поппенгейм» (fon-Poppengeym): the imperial marshal at Constance was Haupt von Pappenheim; rendered as printed, 'von Poppenheim'

Source observation: [22] «Тогда палачи зажгли костер» (Togda palachi zazhgli koster, 'Then the executioners lit the pyre') follows the flame and Hus's falling silent; it reads as displaced (by sense it belongs after [20]); translated where printed
Source observation: [24] «мы не может знать» has «может» (mozhet, 'can', 3rd sg.) for «можем» (mozhem, 'we can'); translated 'we cannot know'
